A1.justification: Both PDFs describe AgentRM and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–D. Corresponding methods and experiments can be matched reliably across the revision.

before.justification: v1 reports original agent evaluations, reward-model ablations, scaling experiments, general-reasoning results, and reward-preference accuracy in Appendix D.2.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds policy-model transfer evaluations and a comparison of policy versus reward training at matched example counts.

M1.justification: The implemented SFT sampler, MCTS annotation, three reward-modeling approaches, objectives, Best-of-N sampling, and beam search remain unchanged. Section 3.1 adds an explanation that behavior cloning is optional with a sufficiently capable sampler; it does not report replacing the implemented pipeline.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same nine agent tasks, Alfworld perturbations, and GSM8k, MATH500, and Codecontests evaluations. v2 enumerates tool subdomains and clarifies held-in versus held-out environments, without documenting additional dataset or task coverage.

E2.justification: v2 adds ATLAS to Table 1 and MPO and GLIDER to Table 2, retaining the previous comparators. Figure 3 also adds standalone policy training as a comparator to the existing reward-training scaling curve.

E3.justification: The retained evaluation gains LLaMA-3.2-1B, LLaMA-3.2-3B, and Qwen2.5-14B configurations. Section 5.2 adds policy-training controls at approximately 4k and 48k examples, collecting successful MCTS trajectories for the enlarged set. Existing dataset splits, metrics, search settings, and Appendix B hyperparameters remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The revision substantially expands evidence about the central training choice and transferability. Section 5.2 adds a matched-example-count comparison of policy and reward training, while Section 5.4 extends transfer analysis from two to five policy models across additional sizes and a new model family. Existing perturbation, state-representation, and appendix preference analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Table 3 retains the same standard deviations across perturbation conditions. Neither version reports experimental seed counts, repeated-run uncertainty, confidence intervals, or significance tests; the added results introduce no new statistical reporting practice.

E6.justification: Substantial results are added while existing table entries remain unchanged. Table 4 adds reported overall gains of 7.2, 6.8, and 2.9 for Qwen2.5-14B, LLaMA-3.2-3B, and LLaMA-3.2-1B, respectively, including a Qwen ToolQuery decrease from 80.0 to 48.3. New baseline scores, Figure 3 policy-training results, and the Section 3.1 sampler-comparison footnote further extend the reported evidence.

T1.justification: The POMDP formulation, SFT objective, UCB selection rule, value backpropagation, MSE loss, and implicit reward log-ratio equation are unchanged. No new theorem, proof, or substantive mathematical derivation is introduced.

C1.justification: The core reward-guided agent-generalization claim remains. v2 explicitly characterizes generalization as handling unseen tasks requiring novel optimal behavior in the abstract, and replaces the introduction's comparative efficiency claim about explicit versus implicit reward modeling with a broader scalability statement.

C2.justification: Section 5.7 is reframed around preserving general-reasoning capabilities and removes the broader general-purpose reward-model interpretation. v2 adds the matched-data scalability interpretation and qualifies when behavior cloning can be omitted. The limitations replace the discussion of constrained MCTS sampling with deferred policy reinforcement learning, although the MCTS settings remain documented.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly identifies the reward backbone as LLaMA3-8B-Instruct and replaces a future code-release promise with an announced code-and-data release and repository address. Appendix B's implementation details remain unchanged. However, new captions claiming LLaMA3-8B-Instruct for all methods conflict with Appendix C's retained LLaMA-2-chat attribution for QLASS, so a baseline backbone change is not established.

R1.justification: v2 adds citations for ATLAS, MPO, GLIDER, Hephaestus, automatic reward modeling and planning, internalized utility judgment, and group-in-group policy optimization. These update the surrounding literature without substantially changing the related-work organization or the claimed novelty of a generalizable agent reward model.

P1.justification: The abstract, introductory motivation, and conclusion receive limited rewrites; explanations of initialization and task coverage expand. Sections 5.4 and 5.7 are renamed, and affiliations, contact information, and acknowledgments are updated. The main section order and most method and appendix prose remain intact.

P2.justification: Figure 3 gains a policy-training curve, legend, and broader vertical scale. Tables 1–2 gain comparator rows, Table 4 expands, and several displays move with the text. Figures 1, 2, 4, and 5 are unchanged. Caption edits include a clearer Table 8 source note but an erroneous Table 2 reference to Table 6.

improvement.justification: The added training controls and broader policy-transfer results strengthen empirical support, while the narrower general-reasoning interpretation improves calibration. These gains are limited by reporting inconsistencies: the retained four-point superiority claim is not reconciled with ATLAS's newly reported 64.9 versus AgentRM beam search's 63.3 in Table 1, where training coverage differs, and the new backbone captions contradict Appendix C. The additional evidence supports a modest net improvement.
